From the given circuit:
- A $+5\text{V}$ source is connected via a $1\text{k}\Omega$ resistor to node $V_{O1}$, which is grounded through a silicon ($	ext{Si}$) diode.
- Assuming the silicon diode is forward-biased, the voltage at node $V_{O1}$ is clamped at the diode forward drop: $V_{O1} = 0.7\text{ V}$.
- Current $I$ from the $+5\text{V}$ source:
  $$I = \frac{5\text{ V} - V_{O1}}{1\text{ k}\Omega} = \frac{5 - 0.7}{1000} = \frac{4.3\text{ V}}{1000\, \Omega} = 4.3\text{ mA}$$
- From node $V_{O1}$, current flows through the second $1\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor to node $V_{O2}$ connected to a germanium ($	ext{Ge}$) diode.
- Assuming the germanium diode is forward-biased, the voltage at node $V_{O2}$ is clamped at: $V_{O2} = 0.3\text{ V}$.
- Current $I_1$ through the second resistor:
  $$I_1 = \frac{V_{O1} - V_{O2}}{1\text{ k}\Omega} = \frac{0.7\text{ V} - 0.3\text{ V}}{1000\, \Omega} = \frac{0.4\text{ V}}{1000\, \Omega} = 0.4\text{ mA}$$

**Summary of results:**
- $I = 4.3\text{ mA}$
- $I_1 = 0.4\text{ mA}$
- $V_{O1} = 0.7\text{ V}$
- $V_{O2} = 0.3\text{ V}$
proTip: Always check the diode barrier potentials ($0.7\text{ V}$ for $	ext{Si}$ and $0.3\text{ V}$ for $	ext{Ge}$) to find node voltages directly.
